hero.h1:
Hear the author out.
Then see what the sources say.
hero.allowance: Free to start: 10 briefs and 2 Dig Deepers a month, no account.
hero.sub: Save anything you mean to read later. The Lede reads it, renames it for what it actually argues, and makes its strongest honest case, so you know if it’s worth your time. When it is, Dig Deeper looks in the research and the reporting around it and lists every source.

film.name: A short film about The Lede
film.transcriptLink: Read the film line by line
film.transcriptIntro: The film sets its words on paper, one line at a time, and a simple drawing acts out each one. A single orange dot stands for the lede.

lines.words: Everything comes at us at once.
lines.drawing: Gray dots pour in from every edge until the page is crowded.

lines.words: How do we make sense of any of it?
We save it to make sense of later.
lines.drawing: A few drop into a pile at the bottom.
The pile keeps growing and grays over.
A heavy black bar lands on the pile, and everything under it blurs.

lines.words: And hot takes that thrive on outrage.
lines.drawing: The bar cracks into shards that spin faster until the page goes dark.
In the dark, the spinning stops and the shards lie flat as quiet lines.
A slim marker moves along every line.
The first orange dot rises through the lines.

lines.words: So we know if it’s worth our attention.
lines.drawing: The heavy bar shrinks to a short plain line beside the dot.
The lines slide off the page. The dot holds, then fades.

lines.words: When it is, we dig deeper.
lines.drawing: A new orange dot drops one fine thread down.

lines.words: It looks in the research and the reporting.
lines.drawing: Threads fan out to gray dots at the edges.
Each far dot gets a number, and the threads pull taut.
On a dark page, the orange dot alone.

lines.words: Then see what the sources say.
lines.drawing: One by one, light runs along each thread from a far dot back to the orange dot.
The threads let go. One orange dot, still.

lines.words: The Lede · Check everything you read.

signup.requirements: Requires iOS 26 or later. On the App Store in the United States.
signup.closingHeading: Start with the next thing you save.
signup.closingSub: Nothing to sign up for and no password to make. Your library lives in your own iCloud. The free edition gives you 10 briefs and 2 Dig Deepers a month. Check everything you read with Membership. It gives you 150 Dig Deepers a month, and the desk reads it all. It starts with a 7-day free trial.

notes.heading: Occasional notes from the desk
notes.sub: A short note when something meaningful ships. No launch spam; the launch is over.

showcase1.heading: Know if it’s worth your time.
showcase1.body: Every save comes back renamed for what it actually argues and filed on its beat, with the headline it ran under kept beside it. Some you’ll read tonight. Some you’ll know you don’t need to.
showcase1.exhibitAria: A headline, renamed by The Lede
showcase1.exhibitRanAs: A Glass of Red Wine Equals an Hour at the Gym, New Study Finds
showcase1.exhibitLede: The “wine equals a workout” study was run on rats.
showcase1.shotAlt: The Lede’s queue on iPhone: four saved stories, each renamed for what it’s actually about and filed on its beat, with the original headline kept underneath.

showcase2.heading: When it is, dig deeper.
showcase2.body: Every brief starts by hearing the author out: the strongest honest case the piece makes. When a piece is worth more of your time, tap Dig Deeper. The desk looks in the research and the reporting around it, sets out what others found and where the desk lands, and lists every source it wrote from, each one a link to the original. It can get one wrong, so check the ones that matter to you. Run it on a news story, a how-to, or the history thread you fell into at midnight.
showcase2.featureHeading: It finds the reporting under the opinion.
showcase2.featureBody: The Lede reads every source as it is. It doesn't rank outlets and it reads every one. The one thing it changes: when a piece is opinion, it builds the brief from the original reporting underneath, and shows you the reporting it used. Same rule for every publication. More on how The Lede handles sources.
showcase2.exhibitRename: The “wine equals a workout” study was run on rats.
showcase2.exhibitBody: Rats got resveratrol, far more than a glass of wine holds. The study’s lead author says it used no red wine.

founderNote.quote: “I built The Lede because I got tired of headlines that bury the story, or sell one that isn’t there.”
